doc.title: Adapters
doc.paragraph: This chapter goes over the various Adapters, how and when each should be used, and how to configure them.

section.title: Adaptive Framework Core
section.paragraph: This adapter is a special adapter, because it always exists and there is only one instance of its type. This adapter is provided by the Adaptive Framework Core and uses the adapterId of "afw". It presents objects that have been compiled into memory and also generates runtime objects that exist from configurations and environment. Objects from the Core adapter are read-only.

section.title: File
section.paragraph: This adapter allows adaptive objects to be stored in the native file system as directories and files.

section.title: LDAP
section.paragraph: This adapter provides access to adaptive objects stored in Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) compliant databases.

section.title: LMDB
section.paragraph: This adapter allows adaptive objects to be stored in the memory-mapped key-value database, LMDB.

section.title: Model
section.paragraph: This is a special adapter that's used to support mapping objects based on model adaptive object types to one or more objects from another adapter.

section.title: VFS
section.paragraph: The VFS (Virtual File System) adapter, provided by the afw_vfs extension, exposes host files and directories as adaptive objects of type _AdaptiveFile_vfs. Use it when scripts or services need adapter-style CRUD on filesystem content rather than stream I/O via open_file and rootFilePaths.

list.item: Object type _AdaptiveFile_vfs only. Directory objectIds end with /; regular files do not.
File content is the data property (UTF-8 string or hexBinary). Directories list entry names in data. Omitted data on add/replace of a file defaults to an empty file.
Reads and writes load or replace the entire file (subject to maxReadBytes). Writes use a temporary file then rename so shorter content does not leave stale bytes.
Optional markExecutable patterns mark matching vfsPaths executable after write (platform permitting).
retrieve_objects supports adapter-specific options: subdirectory, recursive, suffix, and includeHidden.

section.title: vfsMap and paths
section.paragraph: Configure one or more vfsMap entries of the form objectId_prefix=host/directory/. An empty prefix maps the adapter root. Non-empty prefixes must end with /; host paths must exist as directories and end with / (a trailing backslash is accepted on Windows).

For any objectId, the map entry with the longest matching prefix is used (path boundary matching, same idea as application rootFilePaths). Host roots are canonicalized at adapter start; resolved host paths must stay under that root. ObjectIds must not contain path segments . or .., or backslash.

When subdirectory is set on retrieve, only map entries whose prefix matches that path are used; the remainder after the prefix is resolved under that entry's host directory (the map key is not applied twice to the host path).
Names beginning with . are hidden from directory listings and retrieve by default; set includeHidden to include them. Directory delete is non-recursive (the directory must be empty).

The VFS adapter is not a security boundary against a hostile host filesystem (for example, pre-existing symlinks under a map root may be followed when reading). Prefer trusted map roots and trusted objectIds.
